topics.reference_answer: Deep learning has rapidly advanced extreme weather event prediction. Three key themes: (1) Climate data-driven models: GraphCast (DeepMind), FourCastNet (NVIDIA), Pangu-Weather (Huawei), and ClimaX (Microsoft) all train on ERA5 reanalysis data and outperform or match ECMWF on medium-range forecasts. WeatherBench 2 provides standardized benchmarks. (2) Extreme-event forecasting: GraphCast explicitly demonstrates improved tropical cyclone tracking; NowcastNet targets extreme precipitation; probabilistic approaches improve extreme event recall. (3) Uncertainty quantification: deterministic DL models often underestimate extreme events; ensemble methods and probabilistic models (e.g., diffusion-based) address this. Key limitation: DL models perform less well on unprecedented extreme events outside the training distribution; physical constraints remain important.
